prompts.text: What's one question about your younger self you wish I had asked before now?
Tell me about a school day which shaped the way you respond to challenges.
We come across a photograph of you as a teenager. Which part of the story behind it would you share first?
Childhood interests sometimes return in adulthood once people have time and freedom to revisit them.
Revisit an old hobby together or help each other find one entirely new interest?
Growing older shouldn't mean giving up the activities which once made you curious.
What did you once expect adulthood to feel like which turned out differently?
Describe a time an adult trusted you with responsibility before you felt ready.
We meet someone from your childhood who remembers a side of you I don't know. What would you hope to hear?
Look through old school photographs or read entries from a forgotten notebook?
Which teacher or mentor gave you feedback you still use?
The words people hear at an important age sometimes remain with them longer than the speaker realises.
Tell me about a person who believed in an ability you hadn't recognised in yourself.
We get a chance to thank someone who influenced your life years ago. What would you want to say?
A thoughtful thank-you sometimes arrives more meaningfully years after the original kindness.
What skill do you enjoy helping other people learn?
Teach me something you know well or let me show you a trick I only recently learnt?
Describe the first time you realised someone looked up to you.
A younger relative asks us for advice about handling friendship pressure. How would you want us to approach it?
Good advice makes room for the other person's experience rather than forcing an answer.
Which everyday skill do you think people should learn before living independently?
Sharing practical knowledge is a meaningful way of caring for someone.
One of us learns a useful household skill from a neighbour. How should we pass the favour on?
Recall a moment when solving a small problem yourself felt unusually satisfying.
Learn basic furniture repairs or practise making simple clothes last longer?
Which object in our house has a design you genuinely admire?
People sometimes choose beautiful objects for reasons which have nothing to do with fashion.
Tell me about something you once made by hand and how you felt when it was finished.
We decide to decorate one wall together. How should we choose what belongs on it?
Displaying memories openly is better than leaving meaningful objects buried in boxes.
If we made a small garden together, what would you want to grow first?
Fresh herbs on a windowsill or flowers beside the front door?
A plant we've cared for starts failing. Would you rather investigate what went wrong or begin again?
Describe a place outdoors which helps you think clearly.
The same outdoor space feels different depending on the weather and the company.
Which season's weather changes your mood in a way you notice?
An afternoon outdoors deserves space in a calendar as much as an organised event.
Sit in a shaded park with a book or explore a new walking path?
We decide to spend a Saturday outdoors but the forecast changes. What's a comfortable alternative?
Tell me about an unexpected animal encounter which made you smile.
If we considered caring for a pet, what responsibility would you want us to discuss first?
People's attitudes towards animals often reflect experiences they had growing up.
A lost pet appears near our door. What would be your first practical step to help it?
Visit an animal shelter to volunteer or support an environmental clean-up?
Caring about animals involves understanding the work behind their wellbeing.
Recall a time you cared for something living and felt responsible for its progress.
Which cause would you choose to support if we set aside a few hours each month?
We volunteer together and get assigned tasks with different levels of difficulty. How should we approach them?
Working alongside others on a shared cause often reveals people's patience and priorities.
Help organise donated books or prepare meals for people in need?
A shared act of service should support a real need, not mainly produce a good photograph.
Describe a time someone helped you without asking for recognition.
What does receiving help gracefully look like to you?
A friend insists on paying us back for a favour we meant as a gift. How would you respond?
People attach different meanings to repayment, gratitude and obligation.
Give useful time to someone or buy a practical item they need?
Offering help is easier when you ask what the other person wants rather than deciding for them.
Tell me about a kind gesture you almost missed because it was so subtle.
What's a courtesy you appreciate in crowded public places?
We witness someone being treated rudely in a queue. How would you want us to respond safely?
A person's response to minor inconvenience often says something about their habits under pressure.
Take a quieter route which takes longer or use a busy shortcut to arrive sooner?
Recall a journey we shared with a stranger whose conversation surprised you.
What helps you stay calm when transport delays disrupt your day?
Giving one another accurate updates is more reassuring than promising an arrival time you don't know.
One of us gets stranded and the other is far away. Which information would help us make a sensible plan?
Practical emergencies test whether a couple communicates clearly before reacting emotionally.
Prepare a shared emergency checklist or keep useful contact details in an agreed place?
Which personal safety habit did you adopt because of a past experience?
Tell me about a difficult moment when someone helped you regain a sense of control.
We face an urgent problem with several possible solutions. How would you want us to divide the thinking?
Keeping your voice steady during a problem is a form of consideration for the people around you.
How do you want us to discuss the lessons from a stressful day once things settle?
Some people want to revisit a difficult event, while others prefer to close it after resolving the problem.
Write down the useful lesson from a mistake or talk it through once and move forward?
Recall a problem we solved which seemed worse at first than it turned out to be.
We realise we've both overlooked an important deadline. What's the fairest way to respond?
How do you notice when you're becoming too hard on yourself?
Treating mistakes as information is more constructive than using them as evidence of someone's character.
Tell me about a failure which eventually made you more patient with somebody else.
Two people share responsibility for a mistake without always sharing it in equal proportions.
I admit I've handled an obligation poorly. What response would help me take responsibility and improve?
Discuss a difficult mistake face to face or begin by writing down how you feel?
Which compliment makes you feel recognised for your character rather than your achievements?
Describe a time you saw someone treat me kindly and it meant more than you expected.
Small promises matter especially when no one outside the relationship is watching.
We commit to helping someone and realise the task is bigger than expected. How should we adjust our promise?
Relationships feel safer when people explain limitations before they become disappointments.
What is one way our communication has become clearer since we first met?
Ask each other one thoughtful question every week or keep an occasional shared journal?
Tell me about a conversation we nearly postponed which you're glad we had.
We find ourselves disagreeing about the same thing repeatedly. What new approach would be worth trying?
Changing how a conversation happens is sometimes more useful than repeating the same argument.
Which part of our partnership are you most interested in learning more about over time?
Tell me about something you learned through our relationship which surprised you about yourself.
We're planning a weekend and realise both of us have kept a personal wish quiet. How should we choose what to do?
People share more freely when they know curiosity won't turn into criticism.
Maintaining a sense of individuality is worth discussing openly throughout a partnership.
Plant a tree to mark a shared milestone or donate books in honour of the occasion?
Which ordinary moment from this month would you want to remember a year from now?
